card: This pull request migrates native Windows builds and CI from MSVC (cl.exe) to clang-cl, dropping support for building with cl.exe. Switching to clang-cl eliminates ongoing maintenance workarounds for MSVC bugs (#31456, #36153) and unblocks inline assembly optimizations on Windows. Author benchmarks show block connection performance increasing by over 50% alongside a 38% reduction in Windows CI build times. Native Windows developers must install the clang-cl toolset via Visual Studio or LLVM.
changed_since_previous: Added commits to clean up CMake feature and introspection checks (atomics, ARMv8/x86 SHA-NI, CRC32C SSE4.2, and Minisketch CLMUL) so they compile warning-free when warnings are treated as errors, and adjusted crypto flags from -msse4 to -msse4.1.

enables: Hardware-accelerated inline assembly on Windows (e.g. secp256k1 #1681)

evidence: Author microbenchmarks demonstrate significant throughput improvements for clang-cl over MSVC on Windows (ConnectBlockAllSchnorr increases from 7.32 to 11.81 block/s, and DeserializeBlockTest increases from 121.46 to 189.04 block/s).
Author CI measurements show Windows build times dropping from 20m 35s under MSVC to 12m 43s under clang-cl.
Closes #31456 and #36153, which document recurring MSVC compiler bugs and failed constant evaluation in requires-expressions.
problem: MSVC (cl.exe) lacks inline assembly support on x64 and ARM64 architectures, produces slower binaries, suffers from longer CI build times, and causes ongoing maintenance overhead due to compiler bugs and internal compiler errors (#31456, #36153).

risk.why: Build system changes affecting native Windows compilation could break builds or produce miscompiled Windows release binaries.

scope_notes: Drops support for native MSVC cl.exe entirely; Windows developers building natively will require Visual Studio with the clang-cl component (VS 17.14 minimum).
summary: Native Windows builds and CI are migrated from MSVC (cl.exe) to LLVM's clang-cl, dropping support for compiling with cl.exe. CMake configuration, presets, diagnostic flags, and introspection checks are adapted for clang-cl, and native Windows binaries are linked against Clang's builtins runtime library. Workarounds for MSVC compiler bugs and constexpr restrictions are removed from source and test files.
